intended_object: A convenience constructor turning a single transition `first → last` into a run of length 1 of the library's own `FiniteRun` type, a length-indexed path for a `Type`-valued transition relation. The docstring only says "GapCVP reduction support".
explanation:
`FiniteRun transition a b n` is an inductive family defined in this file. It encodes a path of exactly `n` steps from `a` to `b`, with constructors `refl` and `tail`. `single h` is just `.tail (.refl first) h`, the one-edge path, built so that it fits the library's length-indexed run type.

The construction is correct: it gives a run of length 1 from `first` to `last` made of the edge `h`. It is also fully general, with no hypotheses on `α` or `transition`. Mathlib's closest analogue is `Quiver.Hom.toPath`, which works on unindexed quiver paths.

Still, it is not a mathematical definition in its own right. It is a helper constructor for an internal datatype that supports the GapCVP reduction proofs, which is what its docstring says. So it falls under "technical device / implementation detail". If it were read as "the length-1 path given by one edge", it would be faithful.
